VTS Scoring Log

Evolve BioPep

evolvebiopep.com · Est. 2019 · US Manufacturer · APA Founding Member · Scored August 2026

Evolve BioPep operates a publicly accessible site (age-gate only, not a real account requirement) and maintains a COA library at evolvebiopep.com/coa-library/ linked directly from the site navigation. The vendor claims full-panel independent testing through ISO/IEC 17025-accredited laboratories covering identity, purity, endotoxins, sterility, and heavy metals - a broader scope than most vendors in this catalog. An EvolvE batch numbering system is used, with each batch approved and assigned an identifier before release. Evolve BioPep identifies as a founding member of the American Peptide Association and describes itself as a US-based manufacturer and distributor. The primary scoring gap is that the testing laboratories are not named by facility name, address, or credentials - the ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation claim and full-panel scope cannot be independently verified without a named lab.

61 /100
Moderate
Public COA library, full-panel ISO/IEC 17025-accredited lab testing claimed (endotoxins, sterility, heavy metals), APA founding member, EvolvE batch system, 7-year operational track record. Held from High band by unnamed testing laboratories and absence of a physical address.

Scoring Notes
ISO/IEC 17025 claim is the highest-stakes unverifiable assertion in this scoring batch
ISO/IEC 17025 laboratory accreditation is a meaningful credential - it means the lab operates under a formal quality management system for testing and calibration. Vendors that use named ISO/IEC 17025-accredited labs (like BioLongevity Labs' SafeCert/CLIA relationships) score among the highest in the catalog. The problem here is the lab is unnamed. A researcher cannot search the ILAC database, the A2LA directory, or any other accreditation registry to verify whether the lab actually holds this credential. The claim earns partial credit; the verification gap limits it to partial credit only.
APA founding membership is a meaningful process signal
The American Peptide Association promotes responsible practices, compliance, and research standards in the peptide industry. Founding membership signals early, sustained engagement with these standards. BioLongevity Labs (94/100, highest score in the catalog) is also an APA member. APA membership is a process signal, not a product certification, and is scored as such.
What would move this score into the High band
Naming the ISO/IEC 17025-accredited laboratory with a verifiable address and accreditation number would materially improve the Third-Party Testing Practice score. If the named lab also maintains an independently searchable COA archive (as Freedom Diagnostics does), the Batch Traceability score would improve further. Those two changes alone would likely push this score above 80.
